paragraphs.english: Rina was preparing a photo page for her class website. She had many pictures from a recent school trip. Her favorite showed three friends laughing beside a river. She wanted to upload it immediately, but the class website leader asked her to check with everyone in the picture first. Rina thought that this would take unnecessary time because the picture looked cheerful.
paragraphs.translation: リナはクラスのウェブサイト用に写真ページを準備していた。遠足の写真が多く、お気に入りは川辺で笑う友人三人だった。すぐ掲載したかったが、担当者は写る全員に先に確認するよう頼んだ。楽しそうな写真なので無駄な時間だと思った。

paragraphs.english: Two friends agreed, but the third asked her to choose another image. [1] Rina had never noticed that the friend's name was clearly visible on a bag. The friend was happy to share memories with classmates but did not want that detail on a public page. Rina chose a picture of the river instead.
paragraphs.translation: 二人は了承したが、三人目は別の画像を求めた。その友人は、かばんの名前が公のページに出ることを望んでいなかった。リナはそれまで名前がはっきり写っていると気づかなかった。級友と思い出を共有するのはうれしくても、その情報は公開したくなかったのだ。代わりに川の写真を選んだ。

paragraphs.english: The finished page included places, food, and pictures that everyone had approved. It still looked lively. Rina learned that asking first did not prevent people from sharing an experience. It helped them share it in a way that everyone could feel comfortable with, even after the trip was over.
paragraphs.translation: 完成ページには場所、食べ物、全員が了承した写真が載り、十分生き生きしていた。先に尋ねても体験共有を妨げるわけではなく、遠足後も皆が安心できる形で共有できるとリナは学んだ。

title: 比べる条件をそろえる

paragraphs.english: Two students wanted to find out whether covering a bowl would keep water from disappearing quickly. They put one bowl near a sunny window and another in a dark corner. The bowl by the window had a cover, while the other did not. After several days, they compared the water levels. They were excited about presenting the difference to their science class.
paragraphs.translation: 生徒二人は、器にふたをすると水が減る速さを抑えられるか調べようとした。一つを日当たりのよい窓辺、もう一つを暗い隅に置いた。窓側にはふたがあり、他方にはなかった。数日後に水位を比べ、違いを発表するのを楽しみにした。

paragraphs.english: Their teacher looked at the drawings of the experiment. [1] The students had changed both the covers and the locations. They could not be sure which difference had affected the water. So they began again, this time placing the two bowls side by side. They used equal amounts of water and checked them at the same time each day.
paragraphs.translation: 先生は実験図を見て、二つの器の場所は同じか尋ねた。生徒はふたと場所の両方を変えており、どちらが水に影響したか確信できなかった。そこでやり直し、器を並べ、同量の水を入れて毎日同時刻に確認した。

paragraphs.english: The second experiment took another week, but the students understood their question much better. Their presentation included both attempts. They explained why the first comparison had been difficult to understand. For them, learning science now included improving a question and a method, not just obtaining an interesting result.
paragraphs.translation: 二回目にもう一週間かかったが、問いをより理解できた。発表には両方の試みを入れ、最初の比較が解釈しにくい理由を説明した。科学を学ぶのは面白い結果を得るだけでなく、問いと方法をよくすることも含むと考えるようになった。

paragraphs.english: For a history project, Kota interviewed two older neighbors about the town's first sports ground. Both remembered playing there as children, but they gave different dates for its opening. One said that it opened when she was seven. The other remembered an opening ceremony several years later. Kota worried that one person must be wrong and that he should remove one interview from his report.
paragraphs.translation: 歴史課題でコウタは高齢の近隣住民二人に町初の運動場を取材した。二人とも子供時代に遊んだが、開設年が違った。一人は七歳の時、もう一人は数年後の開場式を覚えていた。どちらかが間違いで、一方の取材を報告から外すべきかと心配した。

paragraphs.english: He visited the town archive with his teacher. An old newspaper showed a photograph of children playing on an unfinished field. A later article described a ceremony after new seats and changing rooms had been added. [1] The neighbors had remembered different stages of the same place, rather than completely different events.
paragraphs.translation: 先生と資料館に行くと、古新聞には未完成の広場で遊ぶ子供の写真があった。後の記事は座席と更衣室の追加後の式を伝えていた。運動場は公式の開場式より前から使われていたのだ。二人は別々の出来事でなく同じ場所の違う段階を覚えていた。

paragraphs.english: Kota kept both interviews. He used the newspaper dates to explain the difference and asked the neighbors to check his summary. His final report showed how memories and written records could help each other. He learned to ask more questions before deciding that two different answers could not both contain useful information.
paragraphs.translation: コウタは両方の取材を残した。新聞の日付で違いを説明し、二人に要約を確認してもらった。最終報告では記憶と文書が補い合う様子を示した。異なる答えに有用な情報が両方あるはずがないと決める前に、さらに尋ねることを学んだ。

title: 初めて遊ぶ人のために

paragraphs.english: A group of students made a board game for the school festival. Players moved wooden animals along a river drawn on the board. The students tested it many times and thought the rules were easy. However, when younger children tried the game, several could not begin. They did not know how many cards to take or which animal should move first. The makers had forgotten that they already knew these things.
paragraphs.translation: 生徒の班は文化祭用にボードゲームを作った。盤に描いた川に沿い木の動物を動かす。何度も試して規則は簡単だと思ったが、年下の子が試すと始められない子がいた。何枚カードを取るか、どの動物から動かすか不明だった。作り手は自分たちには既知だと忘れていた。

paragraphs.english: The group watched without explaining anything at first. They wrote down every place where the children stopped. [1] The new page showed the starting position and one complete turn with pictures. The children could point to the pictures while they played. A short example was more useful than another long paragraph of instructions.
paragraphs.translation: 班は初め説明せず観察し、子供が止まった箇所を全て記した。そこで遊び始めの例を別紙に作った。新しい紙は初期配置と一回分の手順を絵で示し、子供は遊びながら絵を指せた。長い説明を足すより短い実例が役立った。

paragraphs.english: At the festival, the game table stayed busy. The makers still answered questions, but they no longer had to explain the beginning to every family. They learned that clear rules should be tested with people who have not helped create them.
paragraphs.translation: 文化祭ではゲーム台に人が絶えなかった。質問には答えたが、全家族に最初から説明する必要はなくなった。分かりやすい規則は、制作に関わっていない人に試してもらうべきだと学んだ。

Her friend Ren brought a much smaller bag. Aki thought that he was not ready for changes in the weather. At the meeting place, their guide asked everyone to place their things on a table.
paragraphs.translation: 低い山への日帰り旅行の前、アキは役立つ物をたくさん詰めた。大きな本二冊、予備の靴、ジュース三本、重いカメラを入れた。レンはずっと小さな袋で、アキは天気の変化に備えていないと思った。集合場所で案内役は荷物を机に出すよう求めた。

paragraphs.english: Ren had water, a light rain jacket, lunch, and a small map. Aki's bag contained many things she would probably not use. [1] Together, they checked the route, the weather forecast, and the length of the walk. Aki removed the books and the extra shoes but kept the rain jacket that had been hidden at the bottom.
paragraphs.translation: レンには水、軽い雨具、昼食、小地図があった。アキには使わなそうな物が多かった。案内役は、たくさん運ぶことと必要な物を運ぶことは同じでないと説明した。経路、予報、歩く長さを一緒に確認し、アキは本と予備靴を出したが、底に埋もれた雨具は残した。

paragraphs.english: On the hill, she was glad that her bag felt lighter. When a short shower came, both friends put on their jackets. Aki learned that preparation meant making choices based on the actual plan, not bringing every object that might be useful somewhere.
paragraphs.translation: 山では袋が軽くなりうれしかった。にわか雨の時は二人とも上着を着た。準備とは、どこかで役立ちそうな物を全て持つのでなく、実際の計画に基づき選ぶことだと学んだ。

paragraphs.english: Saki practiced a short piano piece for a class concert. She liked the opening and played it again and again. However, two bars in the middle were difficult. Each time she reached them, she stopped, felt unhappy, and returned to the beginning. After a week, she could play the opening beautifully, but the middle had hardly improved. She began to think that she was simply not good at music.
paragraphs.translation: サキはクラス演奏会用の短いピアノ曲を練習した。好きな冒頭を何度も弾いたが、中ほどの二小節が難しかった。そこに来ると止まり、落ち込んで初めに戻った。一週間後、冒頭は美しくなっても中ほどはほぼ上達せず、音楽が苦手なのだと思い始めた。

paragraphs.english: Her teacher asked her to play only the difficult bars very slowly. [1] Saki noticed that one finger had to move before the next note began. Once she understood the movement, she repeated it several times and then joined the bars to the rest of the piece. The whole song became smoother.
paragraphs.translation: 先生は難しい小節だけをとてもゆっくり弾くよう頼んだ。初めから毎回弾く代わりに、一つの小さな問題を調べられた。サキは次の音の前に一本の指を動かす必要に気づいた。動きを理解して繰り返し、曲の他の部分とつなぐと全体が滑らかになった。

paragraphs.english: She still practiced the opening, but she no longer spent all her time there. Her next week's plan gave extra time to the places that needed attention. Saki discovered that a useful practice session was not always the same as an enjoyable performance of the easiest part.
paragraphs.translation: 冒頭も練習したが、全時間をそこに費やさなくなった。翌週は注意が必要な箇所に時間を多めに配した。役立つ練習は、一番易しい部分を楽しく弾くことと同じではないと知った。

paragraphs.english: The science club planned an evening for families to look at stars. Members borrowed two telescopes and made a list of bright objects to find. On the afternoon of the event, thick clouds covered the sky. Some members wanted to send everyone a cancellation message. Their leader asked whether the evening had to depend entirely on seeing real stars through a telescope.
paragraphs.translation: 科学部は家族向けの星を見る夜を計画した。望遠鏡二台を借り、探す明るい天体を一覧にした。当日の午後は厚い雲に覆われ、中止を知らせたい部員もいた。部長は、本物の星を望遠鏡で見ることだけに夜の活動を頼る必要があるか尋ねた。

paragraphs.english: They moved tables into the school hall and spread out large sky maps. [1] At one table, children practiced finding north on a map. paragraphs.english: A small island received parcels by boat three times a week. When visitors ordered things online, they sometimes expected delivery the next day. A shopkeeper named Nori often heard complaints when packages arrived later. The online message said that an order had left a warehouse, but it did not show when the island boat would leave the mainland. Strong winds could delay the boat even after a parcel reached the port.
paragraphs.translation: 小島には週三回、船で荷物が来た。旅行者が通販すると翌日配達を期待する場合があり、遅れると店主ノリはよく苦情を聞いた。通販の表示は倉庫出発まで分かっても、島の船が本土を出る時刻を示さなかった。港に着いた荷物でも強風で船が遅れることがあった。

paragraphs.english: Nori made a small board beside his shop. [1] He wrote the next planned boat day and added a note when the port announced a change. He did not promise an exact arrival time for each parcel. Instead, the board helped people understand which part of the journey they were waiting for.
paragraphs.translation: ノリは店の横に小さな板を作り、本土の港から届く知らせを使った。次の出航予定日を書き、港が変更を発表したら追記した。個々の荷物の正確な到着時刻は保証せず、行程のどの段階を待っているか分かるようにした。

paragraphs.english: Visitors began asking more useful questions. Rather than saying that the shop had lost their parcel, they asked whether the next boat was running. Nori could not change the wind, but clear local information made the wait less confusing for everyone.
paragraphs.translation: 来訪者は適切に質問するようになった。店が荷物をなくしたと言う代わりに、次の船が運航するか尋ねた。風は変えられなくても、明確な地域情報で待つ混乱は減った。

title: 絵のついた昼食メニュー

paragraphs.english: At the beginning of the school year, students from several countries joined a lunch club. Each Friday, the members ordered meals from a small restaurant. Some students did not eat meat, and others preferred food without hot peppers. The restaurant had many choices, but its menu used words that new members did not know. Asking a friend to explain every dish took a long time. The club leader, Lisa, wanted everyone to choose a meal without feeling embarrassed. [1] She asked the restaurant owner to check each drawing before printing the new menu. A leaf showed meals without meat, and a pepper showed hot dishes. The pictures did not replace the names or descriptions. They helped students decide which descriptions to read carefully. At the next meeting, ordering took less time, and two new members asked questions about dishes they had never tried. Lisa realized that a small change in information could make joining a group easier.
paragraphs.translation: 新学年、さまざまな国の生徒が昼食クラブに入った。金曜日ごとに小さな飲食店から注文したが、肉を食べない人や辛くない料理を好む人がいた。メニューは選択肢が多くても、新しい部員には分からない語があり、友達に全部説明してもらうのは時間がかかった。リサは恥ずかしがらず選べるよう、料理名の横に簡単な絵を加えることを提案した。印刷前に店主に確認してもらい、葉は肉なし、唐辛子は辛い料理を示した。絵は名前や説明を置き換えるものではなく、詳しく読む説明を選ぶ助けになった。次の会では注文が早くなり、新入部員二人が未経験の料理について質問した。小さな情報の工夫が参加しやすさにつながるとリサは気づいた。

paragraphs.english: During a class discussion about school uniforms, Mr. Lee noticed that the same four students answered most questions. Other students listened, but he could not tell whether they agreed or had different ideas. He first tried asking everyone to speak in turn. Several students simply repeated the previous answer because they had not prepared their own words. Mr. Lee changed the next discussion. Before anyone spoke, he gave the class one quiet minute to write down an opinion and a reason. [1] Then students compared notes with a partner before talking to the whole class. More hands went up than before. One quiet student pointed out that buying sports clothes and regular uniforms could cost families a lot. Her idea led to a useful discussion of prices. Mr. Lee kept the writing time in later lessons. He did not expect every student to become a confident speaker immediately, but he wanted everyone to have a fair chance to think.
paragraphs.translation: 制服についての話し合いで、リー先生はいつも同じ四人が答えることに気づいた。他の生徒が賛成なのか別の考えなのか分からなかった。順番に全員を当てると、準備できず前の人の答えを繰り返す生徒もいた。次は発言前に一分間、静かに意見と理由を書かせた。これで生徒は自分の答えを考える時間を得た。その後、隣の人とメモを比べてから全体で話した。挙手が増え、普段静かな生徒が、運動着と制服の両方は家計に負担だと指摘して価格の議論になった。先生は以後も書く時間を設けた。すぐに全員が自信ある話し手になるとは期待せず、公平に考える機会を与えたかった。
